claims: In the US system, Assistant Professor is an entry-level tenure-track position.
In the US system, Assistant Professor is usually held for 5-7 years.
In the US system, Associate Professor is mid-level.
In the US system, Associate Professor is typically tenured.
In the US system, Full Professor is the highest academic rank.
In the US system, Adjunct/Lecturer are part-time or contracted instructors.
In the US system, Adjunct/Lecturer usually focus on teaching without research requirements or tenure.
A PhD or equivalent terminal degree (e.g., MFA) is generally required for tenure-track roles at four-year institutions.
In the US and Canada, "professor" is often used to cover all ranks (assistant, associate, full).
In many Commonwealth nations (UK, Australia), "Professor" is exclusively reserved for the most senior academic holding a chair.
In many Commonwealth nations (UK, Australia), others are ranked as lecturer, senior lecturer, or reader.
Median annual pay for full-time professors in the US was over $100,000 in 2020-21.
